messages:
maria: Hi team — acme-customer reports their monthly token bucket hit 0 (429s) then the UI showed credits back ~15m later while their long-running job stayed connected. Account: acme-prod-78. Can SRE/billing weigh in on why visible credits flipped without a reconnect?

acme-customer: we were sending requests every ~10s from a persistent process. got 429s for ~12m, then UI showed quota back but our process still got 429 until we restarted it. no manual topup on our side.

maria: repro curl they used:
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwkv-large","input":"hi"}'
# executed in a loop every 10s for ~20m
```

incidents-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4321 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-sre.

akshay: thanks. first suspects: quota cache TTL + timing of the scheduled refill job. can you paste the 429 response headers and any gateway logs you captured?

maria: 429 headers we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-quota-state: depleted
x-rw-refill-signal: queued
x-rw-req-id: req_abc123
```
and gateway logs show: refill job triggered at 2025-10-12T14:02:10Z, write to billing DB at 2025-10-12T14:02:11Z, UI cache invalidation propagated at 2025-10-12T14:02:50Z.

akshay: that ~39s gap between DB write and cache invalidation explains a lot. our UI and several gateway components read a quota cache (redis) that has a TTL and is invalidated on write, but invalidation propagation was delayed. long-lived websocket/TCP sessions don't always get a push for refill — they rely on either an explicit push or client poll. if the client keeps sending and relies only on connection state, it can still hit 429 until it either reconnects or polls quota.

jess: billing confirms the refill ran normally at 14:02:11Z (monthly cycle boundary). no duplicate charges, pro-rata rules ok. the write to the quota table succeeded.

akshay: probable root cause: async refill job wrote the new token bucket -> DB ok -> but cache invalidation took ~40s to reach frontends. meanwhile the persistent client didn't poll quota and didn't reconnect, so it continued to receive 429 until its next state refresh.

maria: short-term mitigations for the customer: implement a small retry/backoff on 429 responses and/or poll the account quota endpoint after receiving 429. example:
```
# simple poll every 30s to refresh visible quota
while true; do 
  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/acme-prod-78/quota
  sleep 30
done
```
or reconnect the websocket when you get sustained 429s.

acme-customer: ok will add a reconnect on repeated 429s and add a short poll loop. thanks — we'll report back if it still occurs.

akshay: ops actions we pushed: lowered quota cache TTL from 60s -> 10s for quota keys, and added a short push/notify for websocket sessions within a 2m window after a refill write. deployed to frontends and gateways just now. also added an alert to watch for refill-write -> cache-invalid propagation > 15s.

incidents-bot: SUP-4321 updated: mitigated. Changes deployed: 1) cache TTL reduced, 2) websocket refill push added. Monitoring window: 2h. :white_check_mark:

maria: closing loop with customer and marking resolved on our side. thanks everyone :tada:
